name: FlightScope — API on RapidAPI
description:
See where a flight actually is right now: FlightScope returns a live position profile for flights currently in the air — plus batch lookups and a searchable global airport database — from community ADS-B data (adsb.lol) and the OurAirports dataset. Coverage follows the community ADS-B receiver network — flights outside receiver coverage, or not broadcasting ADS-B, will not appear.

What you get:
- A live flight profile by flight number: position, altitude, ground speed, heading, vertical rate, aircraft registration and type, with the data age stated in every response
- Batch lookup: check up to 100 flight numbers in one call, with a summary of how many are live, not live or invalid
- A full airport profile by IATA or ICAO code — name, city, country, coordinates, elevation and reference links — plus free-text airport search
- Area lookup: every aircraft currently broadcasting within a radius of a point, for maps and situational displays

Key endpoints:
- GET /flight — live profile for one flight number (IATA or ICAO format)
- POST /flights/batch — live profiles for up to 100 flight numbers in one call
- GET /airport/{code} — airport profile by IATA or ICAO code
- GET /airports/search — search airports by name, city or code
- GET /flights/near — aircraft currently live near a location
- GET /aircraft/{icao24} — live profile for one aircraft by ICAO24 address

Batch / built for workflows:
FlightScope is honest about its source: it reports what aircraft are broadcasting now (including a derived ground/airborne phase), not airline schedule data — it does not publish planned times, delays, terminals or gates. For tracking boards, logistics visibility and aviation apps, the batch endpoint counts as a single API call per request, which keeps polling workflows economical.

Access: subscribe on RapidAPI (free tier available); calls are made over HTTPS with your RapidAPI key.
